- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in subsequent forecasts.
- If sentiment drops below 0.5 for 3+ consecutive days, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model frequently underestimates in early 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5–7 days if sentiment swings sharply.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is falling, model often fails to recognize trend continuation; forecast should be adjusted downward by 1–3% to match sentiment-driven bearish momentum.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative; otherwise, allow for lagged correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overcorrect after strong sentiment-driven rallies; apply a “smooth decay” rule: reduce forecast by 0.5–1% per day after peak sentiment.
